title: How does garbage collection work in Java?
shortTitle: How does garbage collection work in Java?
keyPoints: GC automatically reclaims memory from objects that are no longer reachable from GC roots
Mark phase: trace from GC roots, mark all reachable objects as LIVE
Sweep/Compact: reclaim memory from unmarked (dead) objects, optionally compact to reduce fragmentation
Generational hypothesis: most objects die young → young gen collected frequently, old gen rarely
Young GC (Minor): fast, collects Eden + Survivors. Full GC: slow, collects entire heap
GC runs on its own schedule – you cannot force it (System.gc() is only a suggestion)

s1_definition.oneliner: GC traces from roots, marks live objects, and reclaims dead ones. Most objects die young (generational hypothesis), so the young generation is collected frequently and cheaply.
s1_definition.profdef:
GC algorithm:

1. **Mark:** Start from GC roots (stacks, statics). Trace all references. Mark reachable objects.
2. **Sweep:** Free memory of unmarked (dead) objects.
3. **Compact (optional):** Move surviving objects together to eliminate fragmentation.
4. **Generational:** Young Gen (short-lived) collected often. Old Gen (long-lived) collected rarely.
s1_definition.analogy: The bank vault (heap) periodically audits which safety deposit boxes (objects) are still claimed (reachable). Unclaimed boxes are emptied (garbage collected). Recently opened boxes (young gen) are audited frequently because most are temporary.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  new Account() → Eden
    │ Minor GC
    ▼
  Reachable? → Survivor (age++)
  Not reachable? → freed
    │ age > threshold
    ▼
  Old Generation
    │ Old Gen full
    ▼
  Full GC (slow, STW)

  GC types: G1 (default), ZGC (low-latency), Parallel (throughput)
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
GC automatically reclaims unreachable objects. It traces from GC roots, marks live objects, and frees the rest. The generational hypothesis (most objects die young) enables fast, frequent young generation collection and rare, slower old generation collection.

One sentence to remember: GC marks reachable objects and frees the rest – young gen is collected often and cheaply, old gen rarely and expensively.
